topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session, connects it to prior histopathology practicals, and outlines the day's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor viruses and cell transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the historical discovery of oncogenic viruses, how retroviruses capture cellular proto-oncogenes, and the laboratory assays used to test transforming potential.

topics.label: Classification and functional mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer-associated mutations are defined and illustrate their cellular mechanisms through the G1/S checkpoint and dominant negative p53 mutant proteins.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the causes and cellular effects of sequence instability and chromosomal instability, focusing on DNA repair defects and mitotic segregation errors.

topics.label: Multistep tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the stepwise acquisition of mutations in tumor progression and how inherited germline mutations accelerate cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, offers supplementary reading, and previews the next lecture.
